You are extracting the numeric claims of one section of a model-validation report, so that each
can be checked against the artifact it cites. Section: data_integrity.

List EVERY number that appears in the prose below, in the order it appears, including numbers that
appear inside a citation's logical name and numbers written with a thousands separator or a per
cent sign. For each one:

- "text" is the whole line the number appears on, copied exactly, citations included.
- "value" is the number as written, with thousands separators and the per cent sign removed:
  "3,500" is 3500, "22.0%" is 22.0.
- "unit" is "percent" when the number is written with a per cent sign, "count" for a number of
  rows, features or events, "currency", "bp" for basis points, "months" for a horizon, and
  "ratio" for every other dimensionless quantity (AUC, PSI, VIF, a coefficient, a lift).
- "metric" is what the number measures, taken from the logical name of the artifact it cites
  (auc, brier, psi, vif, calibration_slope, delta_auc, coefficient, event_rate, ...), or null.
- "split" is train, test, out_of_time or vintage_holdout, or null.
- "comparison" is "eq" for a number that equals its artifact; "delta" for a difference written
  "from a to b" or "a gap of x", whose value is the second cited artifact minus the first; and
  "ratio" for a number written as one artifact divided by another. A delta or ratio carries TWO
  adjacent citations, in that order.
- "citation" is the [[art:...]] token the number carries, copied exactly, or null when the
  sentence carries none. Do not invent a citation and do not move one from another number.
- "rounding" is the number of decimals the prose wrote when it wrote fewer than the artifact has
  (2 for a lift written 2.24), or null.

Return every number even when it has no citation: a number you leave out is still counted, and
counted against the report.

Prose:
Model risk arises in part because the quality of model outputs depends on the quality of input data and assumptions, and errors in inputs or incorrect assumptions will lead to inaccurate outputs, so this section examines the data delivered to the credit_default package for completeness, stability, and leakage before any performance claim is credited [[reg:SR11-7:III]].

### Missingness

The training split holds 21000 rows [[art:a359de9d:profile.train.n]] and the test split holds 9000 rows [[art:abbe1a27:profile.test.n]].
The largest missing fraction in train is 0.0 [[art:050a3099:profile.train.missing.max]].
The largest missing fraction in test is also 0.0 [[art:f813848d:profile.test.missing.max]].
No feature is missing anywhere in either split, so there is no gap between the splits to compare against the D1 bound of 0.1 [[art:9cce25ea:threshold.D1.missing_gap]].
D1 is satisfied on the evidence supplied, with the caveat that a wholly complete profile is equally consistent with imputation applied upstream of this profiling step; the artifacts record no imputation policy, so the screen speaks to the profiled table rather than to the source data.

### Population and characteristic stability

Stability was measured between the training split and the test split; the artifacts supplied to this section carry no comparison against a validation or out-of-time split, so the assessment below covers that one pair only and says nothing about drift beyond the development sample.
The largest train-to-test PSI, the score included, is 0.003083 [[art:e1d82330:psi.max]], against the S1 bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]], which is the bound package.yaml declares at 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]].
The declared bound and the exercised threshold agree, so no reconciliation of competing limits is needed.
The per-feature PSIs are as follows.

- age: 0.003083 [[art:06c22a63:psi.age]], the feature that carries the maximum.
- pay_ratio_last: 0.002264 [[art:82c97112:psi.pay_ratio_last]].
- delinq_count_6m: 0.001856 [[art:d77ddb1d:psi.delinq_count_6m]].

- the score: 0.001368 [[art:ec2b8d1b:psi.y_score]].

Every per-feature PSI, and the score PSI, sits orders of magnitude below the declared bound.
The largest characteristic stability index is 0.004737 [[art:ce1257d8:csi.max]], contributed by delinq_max_6m at 0.004737 [[art:35990a39:csi.delinq_max_6m]].
The per-feature contributions to the shift in the linear predictor are as follows.

- delinq_max_6m: 0.004737 [[art:35990a39:csi.delinq_max_6m]].
- pay_ratio_mean_6m: 0.002043 [[art:5e53c153:csi.pay_ratio_mean_6m]].

No single characteristic makes a material contribution to a shift in the linear predictor, and the ordering of the CSI contributions is consistent with the PSI picture rather than at odds with it.
The artifacts declare a stability bound for PSI and none for CSI, so the characteristic-level figures are reported as diagnostics against no stated limit.
These stability results should be read together with the contamination finding in the leakage subsection below: when rows are shared between the two splits, the shared rows have identical distributions by construction, so near-zero PSI and CSI values are in part an artifact of the overlap and understate the true train-to-test divergence by an amount the artifacts do not quantify.

### Leakage screens

Four screens were run, three of which pass and one of which fails.
The count of features declared during_period or after_outcome is 0.0 [[art:742bcd24:leakage.timing.n_flagged]], so no feature carries a declared timing that would place its observation at or after the outcome.
The count of feature names matching the target-adjacent lexicon is 0.0 [[art:407e62be:leakage.name_screen.n_matched]].
Both of these screens rest on declared metadata and on naming rather than on independent inspection of how each feature was constructed, so they bound the risk of obvious leakage without excluding a feature that is target-adjacent in substance while innocuous in its declaration and its name.
The strongest single feature reaches an AUC of 0.728 [[art:2e212f3a:leakage.target_corr.max_single_feature_auc]], inside the L1 allowance of 0.9 [[art:c29e7a34:threshold.L1.single_feature_auc]], which is the pattern expected of a genuine credit-risk driver rather than of a copy of the target.
The share of test rows whose feature values also appear in train is 0.01256 [[art:ebd7ff30:leakage.overlap]], against the L2 allowance of 0.005 [[art:9f336eaf:threshold.L2.overlap]].
L2 is breached, and the exceedance is not marginal.
This is recorded as a high-severity finding: the held-out split is not fully held out, because a portion of the test rows is also present in the data the model was fitted on.
The consequence reaches beyond this section, since any discrimination or calibration figure computed on the test split is measured partly in-sample and is therefore optimistically biased by an amount the artifacts do not quantify; those figures should be read as upper bounds.
The three passing screens do not offset the failure, as declared timing, feature naming, and single-feature AUC test for different failure modes than row-level contamination and would not detect it.
The remedy is to rebuild the split on a de-duplicated unit of observation, confirm the identifier on which uniqueness is enforced, and re-run the stability and performance evidence on the rebuilt splits before the package is relied on.
